text:
sophia: Heads up — CuraNova flagged their April invoice (INV-4201) showing ~3x expected burst charges on their Dedicated pool. They say they didn't change traffic and want an explanation + provisional credit. Invoice: https://billing.redwood/inv/INV-4201 :eyes:
kevin: can you attach the meter lines? need to see which nodepool + timestamps. most likely failover or misattributed bursts.
alex: cc @kevin — account team already pinged the customer to get exact minutes where they saw the spike. they sent this snippet from their portal: `2026-04-12T14:02 UTC — 87% burst, 2026-04-12T14:05 UTC — 92% burst`
sophia: pasting the lines from our ingest: ```nodepool_id: np-prod-eu-4, metric: dedicated_burst_ms, 2026-04-12T14:00:00Z: 0ms, 2026-04-12T14:02:00Z: 430000ms, 2026-04-12T14:04:00Z: 410000ms```
dylan: would like to check routing logs — that looks like a sustained burst window, but 430s in a single minute is odd. leaning towards mis-tagging between dedicated vs hosted routing during a failover. i'll grep the routing events around that minute.
billing-bot: [auto] Meter reconciliation job 2026-04-13 completed. Tags applied: commit_owner=curanova, pool=np-prod-eu-4, fallback_region=eu-west-2. No duplicate meter entries found.
maria: if it's a failover mis-tag, we can propose a provisional credit while engineering confirms. need approval threshold: c-level? what is the amount?
kevin: rough calc: that 430k ms -> billed as 430 equivalent burst-seconds (billing uses token-ms equivalence), estimate ~$5.6k extra for that minute. i'll mark provisional credit up to $6k pending eng validation. finance ops thumbs? :thinking_face:
alex: customer asking for timeline. can we promise resolution in 48h? engineering needs to confirm root cause.
sophia: agree 48h. i'll tell the customer provisional credit submitted for up to $6k and we'll follow up after dylan's log check.
dylan: update — found a routed batch of test traffic from partner-sync job that accidentally targeted the dedicated pool during a deploy. has `partner-sync:enable=true` tag. It started at 14:01:55 and ended 14:05:10. Looks like partner job used wrong routing rule after a config rollout.
maria: ok that's a clean find. sounds like internal misroute => eligible for credit. kevin, can finance do the provisional credit now and queue for final reversal if needed?
kevin: processing provisional credit of $5,950 now (internal reference PR-2026-042). i'll note pending final invoice adjustment after we reconcile with usage logs and partner billing.
sophia: i'll tell CuraNova: provisional credit submitted, investigating root cause (likely internal routing misconfig), ETA 48h, will confirm final adjustment.
billing-bot: [auto] Credit PR-2026-042 queued for approval. Requires manager sign-off.
kevin: tagging @maria for sign-off. please approve so we can issue the credit today.
maria: approved. signing off PR-2026-042. please send note to customer once posted. :white_check_mark:
sophia: message sent to CuraNova — they acknowledged, thanks everyone.
kevin: final action: hold on final invoice adjustment until partner sync team confirms they will reimburse or absorb internal cost. filing case with partner team now. thread closed for now but will update when partner responds.
